meta.titleCubeSolver: Cube solver — solve a 3×3 cube step by step online — cv.cm
meta.descCubeSolver: Free 3×3 cube solver: paint your cube's colours on the net and get a short solution (usually under 22 moves) in standard notation, with a 3D view of every move. Nothing is uploaded.

cube-solver.name: Cube solver
cube-solver.blurb: Paint your 3×3 and get a short solution, move by move.

cube-solver.q1: How do I enter my cube?
cube-solver.a1: Hold the cube with the white centre on top and the green centre facing you. Pick a colour, then tap each sticker on the net to match your cube, face by face. The centres are fixed and show which face is which.
cube-solver.a2: Each face of the net is named by its centre: white top, yellow bottom, green front, blue back, red right, orange left. Copy each face as you see it from straight in front of it; the top face is copied with the green side nearest you.
cube-solver.q3: Why does it say my cube is impossible?
cube-solver.a3: A real cube can only reach certain arrangements. If a colour count is off, a corner or edge has colours no piece has, a single corner is twisted, a single edge is flipped or two pieces are swapped, the stickers were copied wrong (or the cube was taken apart). The message says which kind of mistake to look for.
cube-solver.q4: How many moves does the solution take?
cube-solver.a4: The solver uses Herbert Kociemba's two-phase algorithm and returns a solution of at most 22 moves, usually around 19–21. It is short, not necessarily the shortest possible.
cube-solver.q5: How do I read the moves?
cube-solver.a5: U, D, R, L, F and B turn the up, down, right, left, front and back face a quarter turn clockwise as you look at that face. A ' means anticlockwise and a 2 means a half turn. Keep white on top and green in front the whole time.

cube-solver.lead: Solve a 3×3 cube in three steps.
cube-solver.s1b: Hold white on top and green in front. Pick a colour and tap the stickers on the net until every face matches your cube.
cube-solver.s2b: The cube is checked first. If it can exist, the solver returns a short list of moves.
cube-solver.s3b: Step through the moves one by one, or press Play to watch them on a 3D cube, and turn your real cube the same way.

cubeSolver.title: Cube solver
cubeSolver.privacyNote: Paint your 3×3 cube and get a short solution. Everything runs in this page.
cubeSolver.e_count: There are {n} {colour} stickers; every colour needs exactly 9.
cubeSolver.e_corner: A corner has colours no real corner has, or appears twice. Check the corner stickers.
cubeSolver.e_edge: An edge has colours no real edge has, or appears twice. Check the edge stickers.
cubeSolver.e_twist: One corner is twisted in place, which a real cube cannot do. Check the corner stickers.
cubeSolver.e_flip: One edge is flipped in place, which a real cube cannot do. Check the edge stickers.
cubeSolver.e_parity: Two pieces are swapped, which a real cube cannot do. Check that every face was copied correctly.
cubeSolver.preparing: Preparing the solver… (a few seconds the first time)
cubeSolver.failed: The solver could not run here. Reload the page and try again.
cubeSolver.holdNote: Hold the cube with white on top and green facing you, and keep it that way.
cubeSolver.intro: Press Play to watch the solution on a 3D cube.
cubeSolver.hint: Pick a colour, then tap stickers. Keys: 1–6 pick a colour, arrows move between stickers, Enter or Space paints.
